page: Amazon Web Services r8gb.2xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by the AWS Graviton4 processor. Utilizing the arm64 ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 architecture, the instance provides 8 dedicated physical cores clocked at 2.8 GHz with a single thread per core, avoiding hardware multithreading contention. Cache resources include 64 KB of L1 data cache and 2 MB of L2 cache per core, alongside 36 MB of shared L3 cache. Memory capacity is configured at 64 GB, yielding an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8 GB per core. The instance includes 17 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth, contains no integrated GPUs, and includes no local storage, requiring network-attached storage for persistent disks.

Benchmark results highlight exceptional memory subsystem throughput. In synthetic memory testing, the instance achieved a PassMark memory score in the top tier, supported by large-block read bandwidth of 153.41 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 86.39 GB/sec. Compute benchmarks show balanced middle-tier results across stress-ng and Geekbench multi-core workloads, alongside strong single-threaded bzip3 decompression performance reaching 14.47 GB/sec. However, encryption benchmarks and small-scale language model inference yield weaker relative throughput, reflecting limits in specific cryptographic and low-batch tensor operations.

By delivering an 8:1 RAM-to-vCPU ratio with dedicated ARM cores, the instance provides an efficient architecture for memory-bound systems without the overhead of shared compute threads. The configuration is primarily suited for in-memory caching platforms such as Redis, relational and non-relational database services, medium-scale ETL processing, and applications that require high memory capacity relative to compute footprint.
description: Amazon Web Services r8gb.2xlarge is an arm64 memory-optimized virtual machine featuring 8 dedicated AWS Graviton4 cores based on the ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 architecture running at 2.8 GHz. The instance delivers 64 GB of system memory, providing an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio, alongside 17 Gbps of baseline networking capacity. It operates on the AWS Nitro System with zero bundled local storage and no GPU acceleration. Benchmark testing highlights top-tier PassMark memory subsystem scores, sustained large-block memory read bandwidth of 153.41 GB/sec, and solid Redis SET performance reaching 17.97 million operations per second. CPU-intensive and cryptographic benchmarks fall primarily into average brackets. The r8gb.2xlarge is designed for memory-intensive workloads, including in-memory key-value databases, memory-resident data analytics, and intermediate caching layers that require dedicated single-threaded core execution without multithreading overhead.
